links.outcome: Ability of input data drift detection versus performance tracking to detect COVID-19 drift
links.effect: AUROC stayed relatively stable through the first COVID-19 wave, while TAE + BBSD detected the drift (with a delay). Aggregate performance metrics changed less than 3% under synthetic drifts.
links.quote: Our work has demonstrated that data-based approaches to drift detection can detect data drift (both natural and synthetic) in instances when monitoring model performance in aggregate cannot.

links.outcome: Detection of out-of-distribution input shifts using image and output distribution tests
links.effect: TAE + BBSD detected COVID-19-related input drift; synthetic drift detection sensitivity rose with drift size, e.g. 4000 images gave p<0.05 at 40% male enrichment while 500 images never dropped below p 0.1.
links.quote: We observe correlation between the sample size and the sensitivity of drift detection: with a sample dataset size of 500 the p -value never drops below 0.1 and with 4000 images the p -value drops below 0.05 with a 40% increase.

links.outcome: Timeliness of drift detection given sample size requirements for alerting
links.effect: Detection needs about 4000 new CXRs, which may take days at large providers or months at smaller ones, so alerts may not be timely enough for clinicians to intervene.
links.quote: This finding has direct implications for the practical use of drift detection techniques: if it takes days (large radiology providers) or months (smaller providers) to perform 4000 new CXRs, then existing techniques for drift detection may not be timely enough to allow clinicians using the tool to intervene promptly.

links.outcome: Unequal sensitivity of drift detection across patient demographic subgroups
links.effect: A 5% increase in patients aged 18-35 was detected, but a 30% increase in inpatients or patients aged 65+ was needed for significance; detection sensitivity differed across all demographic groups and methods.
links.quote: For example, a 5% increase in the number of patients aged 18–35 is detected by TAE + BBSD, yet it takes a 30% increase in inpatients or patients aged 65+ for the observed drift to be considered significant.

links.outcome: Whether aggregate performance monitoring against gold labels reveals data drift
links.effect: Aggregate performance (AUROC, F1, precision, recall, Brier) was insensitive to drift, changing less than 3%. Per-class metrics were more sensitive but noisy.
